Brennus

[A chief of the Gaulish tribe of the Senones; invaded the Roman State about 390 
B.C.:
 having entered Rome, he found the city deserted, except by some aged senators, who were murdered in their ivory chairs. The Capitol was, however, defended by a garrison, which was saved from a night attack by the cackling of some geese.]
Væ victis!
Brennus consented to leave Rome upon the payment of one thousand talents. Reproached with using false measures, he threw his sword into the scale, exclaiming, “Woe to the conquered!”—P
LUTARCH:
 
Life of Camillus
 (by whom the Gauls were finally expelled).
